rules.title: Degrees of success
rules.summary: Every check has four possible results. Meet or beat the DC for a **success**; beat it by 10 or more for a **critical success**. Miss it for a **failure**; miss it by 10 or more for a **critical failure**. Then a natural 20 improves the result one step and a natural 1 worsens it one step. The dice roller reads rolls this way when you give it a DC.
rules.cite: Player Core — Checks: Degrees of Success

rules.title: Proficiency
rules.summary: A check adds an attribute modifier and a proficiency bonus. Untrained adds nothing; trained, expert, master and legendary add the character's level plus 2, 4, 6 or 8. The sheet stores each rank and works out every total.

rules.title: Attribute modifiers
rules.summary: The remastered rules write attribute modifiers down directly (usually from −1 to +4 at 1st level, up to +7 later) instead of scores. A boost adds 1 and a flaw subtracts 1; at +4 or more, a level-up boost counts as half until a second one makes it a full point. Every check, DC and Hit Point total on the sheet reads these modifiers.

rules.title: Armor Class
rules.summary: AC is 10 + Dexterity modifier (no higher than the armor's Dexterity cap) + proficiency in the armor's category + the armor's item bonus (and potency rune). Raising a shield adds its circumstance bonus until your next turn.

rules.title: Hit Points
rules.summary: Maximum Hit Points are the ancestry's Hit Points plus, at each level, the class's Hit Points + Constitution modifier. At 0 Hit Points a character falls unconscious and gains the dying condition (dying 1, or more after a critical hit), increased by their wounded value.
rules.cite: Player Core — Hit Points, Healing, and Dying

rules.title: Hero Points
rules.summary: Each character starts a session with 1 Hero Point and can hold up to 3. Spend 1 to reroll a check and use the second result (a fortune effect), or all of them to avoid death: lose the dying condition and stabilize at 0 Hit Points. Award more for heroics and great play.

rules.title: Bulk
rules.summary: Ten light items make 1 Bulk (drop the fractions); negligible items do not count. A character is encumbered when carrying more than 5 + Strength modifier Bulk, and cannot carry more than 10 + Strength modifier. The sheet totals the inventory with light written as 0.1.

rules.title: Initiative and rounds
rules.summary: At the start of an encounter everyone rolls initiative, usually Perception; a character who was sneaking rolls Stealth, one who was talking rolls Deception or Diplomacy. Turns go from highest to lowest; a round is about 6 seconds. Each turn a creature gets 3 actions and 1 reaction.

rules.title: Multiple attack penalty
rules.summary: The second attack on a turn takes −5 and any later attack −10; with an agile weapon the penalties are −4 and −8. Pick the attack in the dice roller's Attack option; creature stat blocks list the three bonuses (e.g. +7 [+3/−1]).
rules.cite: Player Core — Encounter Mode: Multiple Attack Penalty

rules.title: Encounter budgets
rules.summary:
Spend an XP budget on creatures by their level relative to the party. For four characters:

| Threat | XP budget | Each character beyond four |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Trivial | 40 | 10 |
| Low | 60 | 20 |
| Moderate | 80 | 20 |
| Severe | 120 | 30 |
| Extreme | 160 | 40 |

Each creature costs XP by its level:

| Creature level | XP |
| --- | --- |
| Party level  | 40 |
| Party level +1 | 60 |
| Party level +2 | 80 |
| Party level +3 | 120 |
| Party level +4 | 160 |
| Party level −4 | 10 |
| Party level −3 | 15 |
| Party level −2 | 20 |
| Party level −1 | 30 |

The encounter builder spends these budgets on Monster Core creatures; an encounter's sheet shows its budget for the party's size and threat.

rules.title: Difficulty Classes
rules.summary:
Simple DCs by the proficiency a task calls for: untrained 10, trained 15, expert 20, master 30, legendary 40. For a challenge tied to a level, use the DC by level:

| Level | DC | Level | DC |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 0 | 14 | 13 | 31 |
| 1 | 15 | 14 | 32 |
| 2 | 16 | 15 | 34 |
| 3 | 18 | 16 | 35 |
| 4 | 19 | 17 | 36 |
| 5 | 20 | 18 | 38 |
| 6 | 22 | 19 | 39 |
| 7 | 23 | 20 | 40 |
| 8 | 24 | 21 | 42 |
| 9 | 26 | 22 | 44 |
| 10 | 27 | 23 | 46 |
| 11 | 28 | 24 | 48 |
| 12 | 30 | 25 | 50 |

Adjust for difficulty: incredibly easy −10, very easy −5, easy −2, hard +2, very hard +5, incredibly hard +10.

rules.title: Calling for checks (GM advice)
rules.summary: Ask for a roll only when the result is uncertain and matters. Name the skill and set the DC before the roll, and decide what each of the four results means: a critical success should feel like more than a success, a critical failure should cost something. The play guide in table mode lists cues for every skill and save.

procedures.name: Encounter builder
procedures.description: Spends the XP budget for a threat and a party (GM Core's encounter-building numbers) on Monster Core creatures: picks a combination of creature levels that adds up to the budget, then a creature for each group. Accept to add the encounter and every creature (from its stat block). Creature levels run from −1 to 21; at party levels 1, 2 and 18–20 the shapes use only levels that exist, so the budget is still spent exactly.
